transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
President Trump's issued an executive order to promote research on women's health, and
Pierre's Maria Godoy has more.
The order establishes a White House task force led by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy,
Jr. and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles.
It also creates a new NIH division that will be tasked with increasing and coordinating
research on conditions that affect women's health through all phases of life.
President Trump said it was surprising the division did not already exist.
Think of it as women's health division, and it hasn't been done, but it's been done under Trump.
The NIH Office of Women's Health Research has existed since 1990.
The order states that office will coordinate with the new NIH division.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
Last year, NIH was among the agency's downsides in the Trump administration's sweeping cuts
to personnel, as well as grant and research funding across the federal government.
In his 2026 request, the president proposed cutting the NIH budget by 41 percent or by
about $19.6 billion.
With just over two weeks left before the midterm elections, time is running out for registering
to vote in some states, and pairs Hansi Lo Wang with some upcoming deadlines.
The window closes today for eligible voters to register or update their registration in
Alabama, Pennsylvania, and South Dakota.
And there's less than a week left until the next major voter registration deadline on
Saturday at some Massachusetts and New York.
Before you know it, it will be Halloween on October 31st, which is also the last day in
North Carolina for signing up in person at the state's early voting sites.
If you're already registered, election officials recommend going to your state's official election
website to confirm your status and contact information before the deadline.
Voters can be removed from lists, especially if they've recently moved, changed their
name, or haven't voted in a while.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
Russia says it is not ruling out a possible meeting between Russian President Vladimir
Putin, Chinese leader Xi Jinping, and President Trump, should the leaders all decide to attend
an economic summit in China next month.
From Moscow, NPR's Charles Mains has details.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed the subject of the trilateral meeting had come
up in talks, but said no specific agenda had been agreed to.
The spokesman was reacting to a Wall Street Journal report that Putin had suggested the
meeting with Trump and Xi to work out a settlement to the war in Ukraine acceptable to Moscow.
NPR has not independently confirmed the story.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters discussions about a possible trilateral summit
had indeed taken place.
Rubio also reaffirmed President Trump's commitment to ending the war.
In recent days, Trump has repeatedly blamed Ukraine for blocking a peace deal and defended
a decision to ease sanctions on Moscow, saying he didn't want to drive Russia away from the
negotiating table.
Charles Mains, NPR News, Moscow.
It's NPR.
After 43 years with CNN, Christiane Amanpour is leaving.
The network says its chief international anchor plans to depart CNN next June.
The 68-year-old Amanpour is also expected to end her PBS show, Amanpour & Co., at the
end of the year, according to a statement shared by CNN.
However, Amanpour plans to keep her podcast, The X-Files, with her ex-husband, former diplomat
Jamie Rubin.
Her exit coincides with new ownership at CNN's Skydance-owned Paramount recently acquired
Warner Brothers Discovery.
The U.S. Supreme Court has agreed to hear a case about a federal ban on home distilling
of liquor.
This year, as Kerry Johnson reports, lower courts have split on the issue.
The case centers on a federal law from 1868 that bars people from setting up home distilleries.
Congress enacted the ban to protect tax revenue.
The Trump administration supports the post-Civil War law, arguing that billions of dollars is
at stake.
More than a dozen states led by Republicans had asked the Supreme Court to hear the issue.
People challenging the law say it amounts to overreach by Congress.
The law says home distilling is a crime that can be punished by as much as five years in
prison and a $10,000 fine.
The justices will consider the case this term, with a decision expected by next summer.
Kerry Johnson, NPR News.
The prime minister of France calling for limited and localized curfews in response to unrest
stemming from public anger over poor school conditions and rising living costs.
I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News.
